holidays.name: World Nutella Day
holidays.description: A global love letter to the chocolate-hazelnut spread. Fans slather it on toast, crepes, pancakes and pretty much anything else that holds still.
holidays.origin: It began in 2007 as a fan-created celebration started by blogger Sara Rosso, and it has been marked by spread lovers worldwide ever since.
holidays.funFact: Nutella grew out of a post-WWII Italian recipe that stretched scarce cocoa by blending in hazelnuts, which were plentiful in the Piedmont region.

holidays.name: National Weatherperson's Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the meteorologists who brave tricky forecasts, surprise storms and the occasional angry viewer after a missed prediction.
holidays.origin: It honors the birthday of John Jeffries, born in 1745, an early American weather observer who took some of the first recorded weather observations from a balloon.
holidays.funFact: Jeffries took weather readings during a 1784 balloon flight over Boston, making him one of the first to record atmospheric data from the air.

holidays.name: National Shower With a Friend Day
holidays.description: A cheeky observance that is mostly about saving water and encouraging people to think about their water use. Keep it sensible and well within the bounds of conservation.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin that has appeared on quirky holiday calendars for years.
holidays.funFact: A typical shower uses roughly 2 gallons of water per minute, so shaving a few minutes off your shower can save a surprising amount over a year.
